title: Nvidia forms industry alliance for open AI security after Hugging Face hack
summary: Nvidia has announced the creation of an industry alliance aimed at improving security for open artificial intelligence models following a recent hack of Hugging Face. The effort will bring together chipmakers, cloud providers, open-source platforms and security firms to develop shared standards, threat intelligence sharing and best practices for protecting models and data.
content:
Nvidia said it is forming an industry alliance to strengthen security around open artificial intelligence models in the wake of a hack affecting Hugging Face. The group is intended to bring together chip manufacturers, cloud and infrastructure providers, open-source platforms, and cybersecurity firms to work on shared defenses and standards for model safety and provenance.

The alliance will focus on several core areas: establishing interoperable security standards for model repositories, enabling secure model provenance and versioning, improving authentication and access controls for hosted models, and creating mechanisms for rapid threat intelligence sharing across providers. Members are expected to collaborate on toolkits and reference architectures that address both software and hardware attack surfaces.

Industry officials said the move reflects growing concern that models and their supply chains are increasingly attractive targets for attackers. The recent breach at Hugging Face underscored how vulnerabilities in platforms that host or distribute models can be exploited, potentially leading to model theft, tampering or misuse.

Nvidia intends to leverage its position in the AI hardware and software ecosystem to coordinate technical workstreams, host interoperability tests and contribute engineering resources. The company also plans to engage with open-source communities to ensure that any standards or tools developed remain broadly accessible and do not impose undue vendor lock-in.

Observers said the alliance could help close gaps between platform operators, infrastructure providers and the developers who build and deploy models. However, they cautioned that success will depend on transparent governance, participation from a wide range of stakeholders, and alignment with emerging regulatory expectations around AI safety and cybersecurity.

Next steps for the alliance include publishing an initial set of security guidelines, establishing channels for sharing real-time threat intelligence, and running joint exercises to validate defensive measures. The effort may also inform policy discussions as regulators look to address risks tied to model integrity and supply-chain security in AI deployments.

For the broader AI community, the initiative signals a growing recognition that technical and organizational cooperation will be necessary to mitigate security risks as models become more central to products and services across sectors.

## Overview

Nvidia said it is forming an industry alliance to strengthen security around open artificial intelligence models in the wake of a hack affecting Hugging Face. The group is intended to bring together chip manufacturers, cloud and infrastructure providers, open-source platforms, and cybersecurity firms to work on shared defenses and standards for model safety and provenance.

## Alliance focus

The alliance will focus on several core areas:
* Establishing interoperable security standards for model repositories
* Enabling secure model provenance and versioning
* Improving authentication and access controls for hosted models
* Creating mechanisms for rapid threat intelligence sharing across providers

Members are expected to collaborate on toolkits and reference architectures that address both software and hardware attack surfaces.

## Motivation

Industry officials said the move reflects growing concern that models and their supply chains are increasingly attractive targets for attackers. The recent breach at Hugging Face underscored how vulnerabilities in platforms that host or distribute models can be exploited, potentially leading to model theft, tampering or misuse.

## Nvidia’s role

Nvidia intends to leverage its position in the AI hardware and software ecosystem to coordinate technical workstreams, host interoperability tests and contribute engineering resources. The company also plans to engage with open-source communities to ensure that any standards or tools developed remain broadly accessible and do not impose undue vendor lock-in.

## Observers’ views

Observers said the alliance could help close gaps between platform operators, infrastructure providers and the developers who build and deploy models. However, they cautioned that success will depend on transparent governance, participation from a wide range of stakeholders, and alignment with emerging regulatory expectations around AI safety and cybersecurity.

## Next steps

Next steps for the alliance include:
* Publishing an initial set of security guidelines
* Establishing channels for sharing real-time threat intelligence
* Running joint exercises to validate defensive measures

The effort may also inform policy discussions as regulators look to address risks tied to model integrity and supply-chain security in AI deployments.

## Implications

For the broader AI community, the initiative signals a growing recognition that technical and organizational cooperation will be necessary to mitigate security risks as models become more central to products and services across sectors.
